meta.title: Operation of TLC Developing Chamber and UV Lamp

sections.purpose: To perform Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) for qualitative identification and purity testing of plant extracts, drugs, and chemical compounds using a TLC developing chamber and UV lamp visualization.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for phytochemical screening, drug identification, and purity assessment practicals.
procedure: Select appropriate TLC plates (Silica gel 60 F254 aluminium sheets or glass plates) and cut to required size using a sharp cutter.
Draw a light pencil line 1 cm from the bottom of the plate as the origin line and 1 cm from the top as the solvent front line.
Using a capillary tube or micropipette, spot the sample solutions at marked positions on the origin line — spot diameter should be 2–3 mm.
Allow the spots to dry completely; re-spot if higher concentration is needed (allow drying between applications).
Prepare the mobile phase (solvent system) as per the pharmacopeial or standard method and pour into the TLC chamber to a depth of 0.5 cm.
Saturate the TLC chamber by placing a filter paper lining inside — allow 15–20 minutes for chamber saturation.
Place the spotted TLC plate vertically in the developing chamber — ensure spots are above the solvent level.
Close the lid of the developing chamber and allow chromatography to proceed until the solvent front reaches the marked line.
Remove the plate immediately when the solvent front reaches the upper line.
Mark the solvent front with a pencil immediately.
Allow the plate to dry completely in a fume hood.
Visualize the spots under UV lamp: Short wave (254 nm) for quenching fluorescence; Long wave (365 nm) for fluorescent compounds.
Mark the visible spots with a pencil under UV light — use appropriate UV-protective goggles.
Apply appropriate spray reagents (e.g., vanillin-sulphuric acid, ninhydrin, iodine) in the fume hood if further visualization is needed.
Calculate the Rf value for each spot: Rf = Distance travelled by spot / Distance travelled by solvent front.
Compare Rf values with reference standards and document observations with plate sketches or photographs.
Record all observations in the practical record book.
precautions: Always wear UV-protective goggles when examining plates under UV light — UV radiation causes serious eye injury.
Never look directly at the UV lamp without proper UV-blocking safety goggles.
Handle spray reagents (concentrated acids) in a fume hood while wearing gloves and safety glasses.
Ensure the developing chamber is properly saturated before inserting the TLC plate.
Spots must be above the solvent level — submerging spots in the mobile phase destroys the chromatogram.
Mark origin and solvent front lines in pencil only — ink dissolves in mobile phases.
Allow spots to dry completely between applications to keep spot size minimal.
Dispose of used solvents and spray reagents as chemical waste as per institutional protocol.
Keep UV lamp surfaces clean and avoid touching the lamp bulb with bare hands.
